root.claim: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time, $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: reduce the product through a chain of changes of representation down to convolution over a polynomial ring, speed up the transforms with two tape procedures, then recover the exact integer

motivation.text: Each reduction turns the problem into one for which the next fast tool applies, and only the transform data movement and arithmetic need to beat n log n; exactness is restored at the end by known rescalings and rounding.

root.salient: The saving is a strict power $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ of the logarithmic factor, with a tiny fixed exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$, below the conjectured $n\log n$ optimum.

motivation.text: Over this ring roots of unity are powers of y, so transforms need only signed shifts and butterflies, which is exactly what the fast tape procedures accelerate; the pointwise ring products are handed to a standard multiplier.
